rationale: C21 plausibly supplied material drafting machinery for the child: both delegate authority vested in the President concerning military personnel, allocate the principal authority among defense officials, and separately assign Coast Guard-related authority to the Secretary of the Treasury when the Coast Guard is outside the Navy. C01 is also strong because it is a concise delegation under the Uniform Code of Military Justice, but it lacks the child's distinctive service-by-service and Coast Guard allocation. C05 contains similar Defense/Treasury allocation machinery but is less temporally and textually close than C21.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The authority vested in the President by Articles 71 (a) and 74 (a) of the Uniform Code of Military Justice ... is hereby delegated
shared_material.parent_excerpt: there is hereby delegated to the Secretary of Defense ... the authority vested in the President by subsection 4 (a)
shared_material.explanation: Both use the same operative formulation to transfer a specifically identified presidential military authority.

shared_material.child_excerpt: except when the Coast Guard is operating as a part of the Navy, the Secretary of the Treasury
shared_material.parent_excerpt: So much of the said authority of the President as relates to members of the Coast Guard Reserve may be exercised by the Secretary of the Treasury when the Coast Guard is operating as a service In the Department of the Treasury.
shared_material.explanation: This is a distinctive parallel allocation of Coast Guard authority to Treasury, conditioned on the Coast Guard's departmental status.

shared_material.child_excerpt: the Secretary of the Army, the Secretary of the Navy, the Secretary of the Air Force ... respectively, as to persons convicted by military tribunals under their jurisdiction
shared_material.parent_excerpt: delegated to the Secretary of Defense ... in the armed forces ... [with Coast Guard authority separately assigned to Treasury]
shared_material.explanation: Both adapt presidential military authority to the jurisdictional division among defense leadership and the Treasury Secretary.
